item.text: I’ll inspect the workspace, then implement and test `merge_files.py` with an external-sort design so memory stays bounded. I’ll also create a virtual environment and `requirements.txt` (likely with no third-party dependencies if the standard library suffices).

The workspace is empty, so I’m building the tool from scratch with only Python’s standard library. The implementation will make two passes over inputs when inference is needed, then perform chunked sorting and a heap-based merge; this avoids retaining all rows in memory.

The first implementation is in place. I’m tightening two edge cases before testing: inference should evaluate a column’s values as a group (so values like `1,2` infer as `int`), and failed `keep-string` casts must remain sortable even when other rows have successfully typed key values.
